meta.title: Crossworks — Across cultures, across borders
meta.description: Crossworks is a South African public benefit organisation raising and distributing funds to communities in forgotten areas across Africa — water, health, agriculture and discipleship.
meta.ogDescription: Across cultures, across borders — promoting the Kingdom of God and the healing it contains.

who.title:
Promoting the Kingdom
and the healing it contains
who.body: Crossworks is a public benefit organisation that focuses on raising and distributing funds for and to communities in forgotten areas, as well as on equipping these communities with agricultural, health and religious knowledge and resources that we, and our partners, are able to provide. We work across cultures, across borders and across social boundaries to promote the Kingdom of God and the healing it contains.

pillars.title: Water & livelihood
pillars.body: Boreholes, ox carts, seed and vegetable gardens that let a community carry itself.

pillars.title: Health
pillars.body: Supporting a remote clinic with equipment, medication and medical expertise.

pillars.title: Discipleship
pillars.body: Training youth leaders and missionaries, and putting Scripture in their hands.

items.title: Kraaifontein Community Centre
items.alt: Shipping containers being placed for the Kraaifontein community centre
items.body: In Kraaifontein, Cape Town, we support a local community with the practical means to develop and empower themselves — including containers used for community events, church, Bible study and soup kitchens. We also assist with a vegetable garden and contribute to basic needs such as housing, clothing and meals as needed.

items.title: Youth Discipleship — Reach4Life
items.body: In partnership with Biblica we train youth leaders in youth discipleship and provide the material in the form of the Biblica Reach4Life Bible. The programme currently runs at Boy Muller Primary in the Kouebokkeveld and Jakes Gerwel Technical School in Bonnievale.

items.title: Boreholes
items.alt: A completed borehole under a thatched shelter
items.body: Many communities in Zambia and eastern Angola still have limited access to fresh water. Some dig holes to reach underground water; others walk long distances to fetch water daily. We identify the communities with the greatest need and co-ordinate the sinking of boreholes together with the local community and donors.

items.title: Ox carts
items.alt: A family with their ox cart on the Zambezi flood plains
items.body: The flood plains on the banks of the Zambezi in western Zambia lie under shallow water for many months of the year, and the area is then unreachable by vehicle. We donate oxen and ox carts to pastors and leaders so they can take their agricultural wares to market, sustain their families, and continue their work in God’s Kingdom.

items.title: Chilombo Clinic & Mission Base
items.alt: The Chilombo mission clinic in eastern Angola
items.body: In eastern Angola one finds the Luvale people — a forgotten tribe in one of the most remote parts of Africa. Masaha Matondo, a Zambian missionary, serves here, where a basic obstetric clinic, a church and a mission base have been established. We support the clinic with equipment, medication and medical expertise, provide seed for vegetable gardens, support the youth discipleship programme, and contribute toward the mission base gaining ownership of its land. In 2027, by God’s grace, we hope to take a team of South African doctors to this clinic.

give.title: Give to the mission
give.body: Your gift sinks a borehole, seeds a garden, keeps a clinic open and puts the Word of God in the hands of people who have never held it. Crossworks is Section 18A registered, so gifts towards our South African projects are tax deductible — a Section 18A certificate can only be issued for projects inside South Africa.
give.footNote: For a Section 18A tax certificate, email your deposit reference and details to info@crossworksmissions.org.
